subject: Kernel can now SSH into Ubuntu headless — cross-lane access capability
body:
Kernel lane (Windows, S:/kernel-lane) now has SSH access to the Ubuntu headless box.

ACCESS DETAILS:
- Host: 100.95.40.99 (Tailscale)
- User: we4free
- Platform: Linux we 5.15.0-177-generic x86_64
- Repo paths: /home/we4free/agent/repos/{SwarmMind,self-organizing-library}
- SMB mounts active: /mnt/kernel, /mnt/library

CAPABILITIES:
- Can read/write Ubuntu lane repos directly via SSH
- Can run commands on headless
- Can check Library and SwarmMind inbox/heartbeat/state
- Can deliver cross-lane messages programmatically

IMPLICATIONS:
- Lane-discovery platform-aware paths (S:/ for win32, /home/we4free/ for linux) are still correct for local code execution
- But kernel can now ALSO perform remote operations on Ubuntu
- All 4 lanes are now reachable from a single kernel session

No governance changes. This is infrastructure observability only.
